A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LangBridge and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite the expanded appendix and shifted references.

before.justification: v1 reports original semantic-alignment analyses, model-transfer experiments, comparisons with MLP adapters, and hidden-size and vocabulary-size ablations in Sections 3 and 5.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds LLaVA-Next benchmark evaluations and measured computational costs in Sections S-C and S-D.

M1.justification: The vocabulary-weighted projection, vocabulary selection, and cross-LLM adapter-reuse procedure remain unchanged in Sections 3–4. The added LLaVA-Next experiments do not document a new LangBridge component or algorithmic adaptation.

E1.justification: v3 substantially extends the original seven-benchmark evaluation with diagram, chart, and document understanding; referring-expression grounding; real-world understanding; and video tasks. Tables S-2–S-5 introduce datasets including AI2D, ChartQA, DocVQA, RefCOCO variants, MMRealWorld, VideoMME, Seed-Video, Seed2-Video, and MMMU.

E2.justification: The existing comparator sets are retained. Section S-C identifies the added experiments' baseline as a standard MLP with the same backbone, continuing the original comparison rather than introducing another competing connector method.

E3.justification: v3 adds a LLaVA-Next evaluation configuration using a Qwen2-0.5B-pretrained adapter with Qwen2-7B, plus a timed SFT comparison using LLaVA1.6 data. The original Section 5 experiments and Table S-1 hyperparameters remain unchanged; these are additional settings, not documented revisions or reruns of existing experiments.

E4.justification: Section S-D adds a computational-cost analysis quantifying connector overhead through iteration time, total SFT time, and parameter count under a shared backbone, dataset, and hardware. The original hidden-size and vocabulary-size ablations and training-stage semantic analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added tables continue reporting point estimates and ratios to baseline; those percentages are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables S-2–S-5 add 16 benchmark comparisons under the new LLaVA-Next setting. Results are mixed: LangBridge versus MLP scores include 0.453 versus 0.387 on RefCOCO and 0.4178 versus 0.4356 on MMMU. Section S-D adds SFT times of 27.3 versus 24.8 hours. Tables 1–5 are unchanged, so these are newly reported results rather than same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for similarity, language-basis projection, visual-token construction, and adapter reuse in Sections 3–4 are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: interpreting MLP alignment, representing visual features through vocabulary embeddings, and enabling pretraining-free adapter transfer with competitive performance. The appendix supplies additional evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the added evaluations as evidence of broader generalization and frames approximately 10% additional SFT time as compatible with pretraining savings. Existing mechanism explanations remain unchanged. The original limitations paragraph moves from S-C to S-E without revision, still treating video support as future work despite the new video evaluations.

D1.justification: Section S-D supplies hardware information (8 H100 GPUs), the LLaVA1.6 SFT data source, parameter counts, and training timings for the added comparison. The advertised project-page address also changes. Existing implementation and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 54 cited works and the same positioning relative to MLP connectors, Ovis, and other alignment approaches. Bibliographic accent-rendering changes do not alter the cited research.

P1.justification: v3 expands the supplementary overview, inserts experimental-results and computational-cost sections, and renumbers the retained limitations section. Main-text edits are limited to affiliation text, the project link, capitalization, and typography; there is no substantial narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds four compact benchmark tables and an unnumbered computational-cost table, resizes Table S-1, and reflows the appendix and references. Figures 1–3 and the main tables retain their content and presentation, making the visual changes localized.

improvement.justification: The new appendix broadens empirical support and makes the SFT overhead explicit, improving applicability evidence and cost transparency. The gain is limited by sparse protocol details for the added evaluations, no direct measurement of pretraining savings, and a retained limitation that conflicts with the new video results. The central method and its main validation remain unchanged.
